newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - THAI NEWSPAPERS - AUG 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - THAI NEWSPAPERS - AUG 8.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The embattled prime minister has moved to head off pressure for his resignation by ordering the state media to seek official clearance before broadcasting news. The move comes amid intensifying speculation Chavalit Yongchaiyudh had gone to see His Majesty the King to tender his resignation. The rumours were based on a private audience that was arranged weeks ago and concentrate on the economy. (BANGKOK POST, THE NATION)

- The prime minister has made a guarded response to a stinging attack on his government by Anand Panyarachun. Chavalit says Anand has the right to his opinions. While Chavalit is reticent, Yingphan Manasikarn, science, technology and environment minister, hit back at Anand, who chairs the Constitution Scrutiny Committee. (BANGKOK POST)

- Chart Pattana will not quit the coalition government though it is facing a crisis of confidence, party sources say. Their remarks follow widespread rumours that the party of ex-premier Chatichai Choonhavan might leave the Chavalit Yongchaiyudh government to press the prime minister to step down in the face of the economic crisis. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Bank of Thailand is to propose the government issue an executive decree to establish a deposit insurance institution. The institution, originally envisaged by the central bank as part of the Financial Institutions Development Fund, will fully protect depositors of the 15 commercial banks and the 33 finance companies. (BANGKOK POST)

- M Group has sold its stakes in three telecommunications companies to United Communication Industry (UCOM), a move that will allow it to shift its focus back to publishing arm Manager Media International. UCOM Director Poosana Premanoch says the details of the sale can not be confirmed until the transaction is filed with the Stock Exchange of Thailand. (THE NATION)
